subject: Supply-chain & CI review: Terraform module provenance, Helm value drift, Ansible idempotency
messages:
From: rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Joao Santos <j.santos@acme.com>, infra.ops@acme.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-10-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Supply-chain & CI review: Terraform module provenance, Helm value drift, Ansible idempotency

Hi Joao and Acme infra team,

Thanks again for hosting the walkthrough yesterday. As we prepare the Private deployment handoff I want to capture three items we observed during the last validation run that need engineering/CI changes before we sign off on the deployment gates:

1) Terraform module provenance: several module sources in your privstack repo are referenced by branch or unpinned SHAs (modules/networking, modules/storage). We need signed provenance or commit SHA pinning for modules that affect network/egress controls.

2) Helm values drift: our CI detected differences between values applied in staging vs the helm values in the repo (notably imagePullPolicy and egress rules in chart values). We captured a small diff and attached a patch for your review.

3) Ansible idempotency: a subset of playbooks fail idempotency on repeated runs (see the attached idempotency report). This causes flaky CI and prevents reliable rollbacks.

Could you confirm which of these you can address in the next 5 business days and share a brief plan for any items that will take longer? We're aiming to require these three items be remediated or mitigated by policy (signed attestations + CI gating) before we enable the private control plane for production traffic.

Attachments: tf-module-provenance-checklist.xlsx (checklist), helm-values-diff.patch (small diff), ansible-idempotency-report.txt (CI run excerpt)

Thanks,

-- 
Rafael Mendes
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai

From: Joao Santos <j.santos@acme.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, infra.ops@acme.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-10-19T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Supply-chain & CI review: Terraform module provenance, Helm value drift, Ansible idempotency

Rafael —

Appreciate the clear breakdown. Quick responses inline and next steps: 

> Terraform module provenance
We currently consume a small set of internal modules via git references and a few from third-party registries. We can pin SHAs for the modules under our control within 48 hours and add attestations to the module registry for the ones we publish. For third-party modules we'll create a replacement plan (vendor or fork+pin) and add that to the backlog; ETA for full third-party mitigation is 3 weeks.

> Helm values drift
Thanks for the patch — confirmed there are a couple of overrides that drifted when the helmfile was templated in staging. We'll accept the patch but will also add a Helm values validation step in the pipeline that diffs runtime-applied values back to repo values before merge.

> Ansible idempotency
We ran the ansible roles in ephemeral CI three times and reproduced a handful of non-idempotent tasks in roles/network and roles/monitoring. Attached is the idempotency run dump with task names and hashes. We'll prioritize fixes for critical tasks in the next sprint and add an idempotency gate (fail on >0 changed in subsequent runs) in CI.

Action items: 
- Pin internal module SHAs and push attestations (Joao) — target 2027-10-21
- Open GH issue for third-party modules and add mitigation plan (Joao) — target 2027-11-09
- Accept helm-values-diff.patch and add validation step to CI (Acme CI team) — target 2027-10-22
- Fix idempotent tasks and enable idempotency gate (Acme Ansible owners) — target 2027-10-28

Attachments: ansible-idempotency-report.txt, helm-values-diff.patch

I'll loop in our CI engineers on the PRs. Happy to sync if you prefer a quick call.

Best,
João
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Acme Corp
j.santos@acme.com

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Joao Santos <j.santos@acme.com>, infra.ops@acme.com
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-10-20T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Supply-chain & CI review: Terraform module provenance, Helm value drift, Ansible idempotency

João / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the action items. A few implementation details from Redwood's side that will help us close the loop and gate the deployment: 

- GitOps gating: we require a signed attestation artifact for any Terraform module that modifies network or storage (an artifact signed by your CI signing key proving the exact SHA used). Please upload attestations to the artifact store referenced in the Confluence doc linked below.

- CI checks: we'll ask you to add two additional pipeline steps before merges to main: (1) terraform-provenance-check which verifies module SHAs and attaches attestation, and (2) helm-values-validate which runs a helm template + diff against a canonical values file. We can provide a small validation script (we'll open a PR on your repo).

- Ansible: for idempotency, please prioritize the network role fixes that cause port-forwarding and iptables changes. If fixes need to be staged, we'll accept temporary feature flags in the playbooks but they must be annotated and gated by the idempotency CI job.

I've opened a draft PR with the validation scripts and a Concourse job example: https://github.com/redwood-inference/privstack/pull/482
Also copy of the supply-chain checklist is attached in case it's helpful.

Attachments: tf-module-provenance-checklist.xlsx

Can we set a quick sync on Friday to confirm the pinned SHAs are in place and the helm validation step is passing in your staging pipeline? Rafael — does Friday 11:00 PT work for you?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager (Infra), Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Joao Santos <j.santos@acme.com>, infra.ops@acme.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-10-21T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Supply-chain & CI review: Terraform module provenance, Helm value drift, Ansible idempotency

Thanks everyone — Friday 11:00 PT works for me.

João: please mark the TF module SHA pin PR with a comment that includes the attestation artifact URL so we can validate it in our gating script. If you hit blocking items on third-party modules, we can accept a temporary firewall rule that blocks the affected path until a replacement is in place (must be accompanied by a compensating control in the ticket).

We'll review the validation PR you opened and test the helm-values validation in our staging run. Appreciate the quick collaboration.

-- 
Rafael
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
